concept_definition: a group of people working together toward a common goal.
All the inhabitants of a particular town, area, or country.
a group of musicians who play music together.
A group of people constituted as the decision-making body of an organization.
A division or office of a large business or organization.
A body of senior government ministers.
a group of students who prepare together
the social group between the rich and the poor
the social group doing manual or industrial work
A smaller group formed from or included within a larger group, often sharing particular characteristics.
A large group of musicians who play instruments together, usually led by a conductor.
A group of people gathered to watch or listen to a performance, speech, broadcast, or other presentation.
A group of singers who perform together, especially in a church, school, or concert.
A person, group, or country that cooperates with and supports another, especially in a shared cause or conflict.
A group of families or households claiming descent from a common ancestor, especially in traditional Scottish or Irish society.
A person, group, or organization competing with another for the same goal, advantage, or prize.
A social group whose members share a common cultural background, ancestry, language, history, or traditions.
A group of people sworn to give a verdict in a legal case, especially by deciding whether someone is guilty or not guilty.
A group of people chosen to judge a competition, exhibition, or award.
The members of a jury considered collectively.
The team or players whose main role is to prevent the opposing team from scoring.
The lawyers and other people representing a person accused in a court case.
A group of three people or things.
A musical group consisting of three performers.
A smaller group within a family, especially within a language family, cultural group, or classification system.
A small organized group within a larger group, especially one that disagrees with other members and seeks power or influence.
A group of people living in the same area or sharing a common identity, interest, or purpose.
A contemptible or worthless person or group of people.
The artists, writers, or other creators who are innovative and experimental and lead new developments in art or culture.
People who are not Muslims; people who do not follow Islam.
A person or team that finishes second in a competition.
All of human society and civilization, considered collectively.
In sports, the team or players who have possession of the ball or other object and are trying to score.
A gathering of American football players between plays to call and discuss the next play.
A group of players and units in American football that take part in kicking plays, such as kickoffs, punts, and field-goal attempts.
The main group of riders in a bicycle race who ride together in a pack.
A group of bicycle racers who have ridden clear of the main group during a race.
A diagonal line of bicycle racers riding close together to shelter from a crosswind.
The progressive or radical faction within a political party or movement.
A person or organization other than the two main parties involved in an agreement, dispute, or transaction.
The people at an organization’s central office who direct and manage its activities.
A person’s ancestral background or the inherited characteristics associated with their origin.
A group of people or organizations that unite to support a shared cause, goal, or interest.
The people who lead an organization, country, or group, considered collectively.
An expedition is the group of people taking part in an organized journey or mission.
A political party or group that challenges and monitors the party or government in power.
A group considered to be the most powerful, skilled, or influential within a particular field or society.
A grouping of sports teams that compete against one another within a larger league or association.
A large ensemble of musicians that performs symphonies and other orchestral music.
The group of woodwind instruments and the musicians who play them in an orchestra or band.
The political party or group with the most members in a legislative body, typically able to control its proceedings.
The political grouping or movement associated with conservative or reactionary views.
The people, groups, or political organizations occupying the most conservative or nationalist end of the political spectrum.
The organized criminal world and the people involved in it.
The people who live in a village, considered collectively as a community.
A person who belongs to the same group, team, workplace, or crew as another person.
Distinct ethnic, national, or cultural groups, especially considered as separate communities.
A person who works with another person or people, especially at the same organization or workplace.
A core group is the small, central set of people who are most committed to an organization or cause.
Human beings considered collectively as a group.
The lawyers or legal team who represent the state or complainant in a criminal case.
A pantheon is a group of highly respected, famous, or influential people associated with a particular field or achievement.
A line of people waiting to receive a service, such as at a service desk or ticket counter.
The group of people employed by an organization, especially those who work for it.
All the people employed by an organization or working in a country’s labor market.
A group of musicians, singers, or performers who perform together.
A small group of instruments or voices performing together, or a piece of music written for such a group.
The people who live in a particular district or area.
A distinct, exclusive social group or class, especially one regarded as having high status or privileges.
A group of singers who perform together, especially one that sings with an orchestra or in a musical production.
A group of people assembled together, especially for a religious service or meeting.
The people who regularly attend or belong to a particular church or religious community.
Soldiers who fight on foot, especially as a branch of an army.
A military unit made up of several divisions, or a large organized branch of an armed force.
A group of people organized for a particular purpose or belonging to a particular profession or activity.
A large, disorderly crowd of people, especially one that is angry or violent.
An organized criminal group, especially one involved in racketeering or other illegal activities.
The people living in a particular country, area, or community, considered as a group.
A member or supporter of the Republican Party, especially the major political party in the United States.
A group of people descended from a common ancestor, especially one regarded as forming a family line or branch.
A community of people living outside their ancestral or national homeland, often retaining cultural ties to it.
A group of people, especially young people, who spend time together or share an interest.
An organized group of criminals, often involved in violence or illegal activity.
The social class of people who own businesses, property, or the means of production, especially when contrasted with workers; in Marxist theory, the capitalist class.
The middle class, especially people regarded as conventional, materialistic, or concerned with respectability and property.
A particular set of beliefs, especially religious or political beliefs; a religious denomination or group.
The social class of wage earners who own little or no productive property and must sell their labor to live, especially as described in Marxist theory.
A permanent military unit, usually made up of several battalions and commanded by a colonel.
A military force made up of ordinary citizens who are called to serve, especially in an emergency, rather than full-time professional soldiers.
An armed group of civilians, often operating outside the regular armed forces and sometimes without official authorization.
A group of soldiers, especially a unit of cavalry or a body of soldiers organized for a particular purpose.
A group of people or organizations formed to pursue a shared purpose, interest, or activity.
A group of actors who perform together in a play, film, or other production.
The group of people who hold power or influence in a society, institution, or profession, and who are seen as defending its existing order.
A person or group of people who live together in the same home, often including a family and others who share domestic arrangements.
Workers considered collectively, especially as a social or economic group, or the people available to work.
The people responsible for running or directing an organization, business, or group.
A group of people identified by shared characteristics, especially for research, marketing, or statistical analysis.
Soldiers who fight while mounted on horses; historically, the branch of an army that uses horses for mobility and combat.
The judges of a country or court system considered collectively.
A group of people chosen or appointed to make, change, and repeal laws for a country, state, or other political unit.
A group of people or things considered together, especially an informal or loosely organized group.
A group of people chosen to discuss, judge, advise on, or make decisions about a particular subject or case.
A small, simplified crew or staff kept to perform essential duties, especially when most of the usual workforce is absent.
An organized group or association of people united by a shared interest, purpose, or identity, especially a fraternal organization.
A group of people representing an organization, country, or other body, especially at a meeting, event, or military operation.
A group of people chosen or authorized to represent others, especially at a meeting, conference, or government body.
A professional sports team, especially one that is a member of a league and holds a continuing place in it.
A group of people accepted into an institution, program, or organization at one time; also, the number accepted.
A large crowd of people gathered together.
The people who work for an organization, especially its employees considered as a group.
A group of people from the same country or community living together in a place away from their homeland.
An official group of people appointed to investigate, advise, or carry out a particular task.
All human beings considered collectively; the human race.
Human beings, especially in contrast with other living creatures or with the divine; humanity as a kind of being.
A distinct part of a market, audience, or population considered as a group with shared characteristics.
The people who manage an organization or institution, especially its executive officials or governing staff.
A named alliance of states, especially the Axis powers that opposed the Allies in World War II.
A succession of rulers from the same family, especially one that governs a country or region over several generations.
Workers considered collectively, especially as a social or economic group, or the workforce available for employment.
A group of people sent by a government or organization to another country or place for a specific purpose, or the work they are sent to do.
A social group whose members share ancestry, culture, language, or territory, often with a recognized leader or governing structure; especially a traditional or Indigenous people.
A group of people who share a strong common interest, identity, or characteristic, especially as a close-knit community.
The body of people ordained or authorized to perform religious services and duties in a religion or religious organization.
A relatively small group whose members are devoted to a leader, belief, or practice, often characterized by strong control over members and separation from wider society.
A group of people who share a set of religious beliefs, especially one that has separated from a larger religion or is regarded as outside its mainstream.
A group or faction within a larger political, philosophical, or other movement, distinguished by particular beliefs or practices.
The newspapers and journalists collectively, considered as a source of news and public information.
A group of people gathered together, especially for a meeting, ceremony, or shared purpose.
A group of people who work together, often cooperatively or toward a shared goal, and may jointly own or manage an enterprise.
A group of people who work together, especially on a ship, aircraft, or other vehicle.
A team of rowers and, sometimes, the boat they compete in; also the sport of competitive rowing.
A group of people who regularly associate or work together, especially a group of friends or a gang.
A group of people who perform together, especially in a dance or music style such as hip-hop.
A unit or team of workers assigned to a particular task, such as road, construction, or maintenance work.
A group of people working together to operate or produce a film, television program, or theatrical production.
The human race; people considered collectively.
All the people who belong to a particular group, organization, or club, considered together.
A group of people who are smaller in number than another group or the rest of a population, especially one distinguished by characteristics such as ethnicity, religion, or language.
A smaller group of members in a legislative body, committee, or other organization, especially one that is opposed to or distinct from the group in control.
